claims.text: Codd's relational model, published in Communications of the ACM in 1970, volume 13, pages 377 to 387, introduced relations in a normal form in which each relation carries a designated primary key. Its opening argument is data independence: users of large data banks must be protected from having to know how the data is organised in the machine, so that applications remain unaffected when the internal representation changes.

source.title: E. F. Codd, A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks, Communications of the ACM 13(6):377-387, June 1970, doi 10.1145/362384.362685

claims.text: Fellegi and Sunter gave record linkage its decision-theoretic formalisation in the Journal of the American Statistical Association in 1969, volume 64, pages 1183 to 1210, formalising the earlier approach of Newcombe and colleagues from 1959. Comparing a pair of records yields one of three decisions — link, non-link, or possible link — and their fundamental theorem shows the optimal procedure is a likelihood ratio test, which minimises the number of pairs left as possible links while holding two error rates at stipulated levels: linking records that do not match, and failing to link records that do.
tokens: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source.title: Ivan P. Fellegi and Alan B. Sunter, A Theory for Record Linkage, Journal of the American Statistical Association 64(328):1183-1210, December 1969, doi 10.1080/01621459.1969.10501049

beats.broke: two rows can describe the same thing without being the same row, so the count of distinct things in a table is not the count of its rows and cannot be recovered by comparing rows for equality
beats.fix: declare a key — the field or combination that identifies the thing rather than the record — and where no such field exists, treat matching as a decision problem with two error rates rather than as a comparison
beats.cost: an exact comparison finds only the duplicates that were already identical, and every probabilistic method trades the two errors against each other: no threshold removes both, so the choice is which of the two you would rather make
beats.interview: why dropping exact duplicates can leave the totals still failing to reconcile
